posts.cooked:
Please follow the format in How to post a Feature Request

Be as specific as possible, give your post a clear and descriptive title, and focus on problems and use cases, rather than proposed solutions.

As a Roblox developer, it is currently too hard to …

Recently Roblox added studio_id to the MCP ecosystem and this has made running multiple studio sessions with multiple Claude Code agents at the same time workable in a safe way (with some custom automation). But now the human is the biggest problem - I simply am not reliable at differentiating which Studio session I’m currently looking at. So I have to ask Claude to tell me what marker to look for in Explorer to confirm that I’m in the right studio instance before launching a playtest or saving the rbxl to disk. It’s too hard to quickly remember which Studio session is which.

I propose that being able to annotate the Studio top bar with both a name and a color would allow for quick and easy distinction. I’m exploring ways to do this with plugins instead, but it seems like it’s a feature that probably warrants first class support at some point soon.

If Roblox is able to address this issue, it would improve my development experience because …
I will make fewer mistakes working in the wrong Studio instance and I will not have to spend expensive human time looking for markers created by a specific Claude and replicated into a specific studio from that Claude’s clone of the git repo through that Claude’s rojo instance.

posts.name: DistortedByTime
posts.cooked:
I’m happy to share my full Claude plan file, but I don’t know how to do that privately and I’m not sure you want it. I’ve copied the section that I think is most critical to your question.

The key things that need to be synchronized:

  • Which git clone of the repo is a Claude session bound to (can be inferred by path)
  • Which rojo instance is serving the git clone for a particular Claude session
  • Which studio instance is bound to which rojo instance and thus to which Claude instance

Relevant note:
We have a Rails style up/down migration piece of infrastructure that makes prefab creation and assembly reversible and idempotent and when we apply a migration we do write an updated copy of the rbxl to git-lfs. We haven’t figured out how to headlessly run our migrations, which means that we can’t just run the prefab migrations in CI/CD.

## Context

Roblox changed the Studio MCP server from an **implicit active-instance** model to **explicit
per-call addressing**: every tool now requires a `studio_id` from `list_roblox_studios`, and
`set_active_studio` was **deleted**. No KSS skill threads `studio_id`.

That is the trigger, not the problem. The problem is that KSS is developed from **parallel clones
(`KSS/`, `KSS2/`, `KSS3/`), each on its own branch, each with its own Studio session open on the
same place, all mutating concurrently** — the owner has ruled this the working model the project
exists to support (F23). In that setting a migration or attribute write can land in the wrong
session; the developer then hits `File > Save` and commits. Nothing errors. It compounds with the
local-`.rbxl`-vs-Roblox-cloud split (CLAUDE.md §Git LFS): the two stores are independent, so "it
looked right in Studio" proves nothing about which one was written.

### The reframe that shaped this plan

Three identities were being conflated. Separating them is what makes the design tractable:

| | Identity | Question | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|
| **I1** | which MCP connection | which session do my calls reach | D2 — resolve per operation, prove in-payload (the D4 shim alternative is dropped) |
| **I2** | which Rojo feed supplies the scripts | **whose `up.luau` executes** | D1 precondition |
| **I3** | which backing store `File > Save` writes | **what gets committed** | D3 — detection only |

**The harm is an I3 failure.** No MCP-layer control can prevent it, because the Save is performed
by a human. D3 therefore detects rather than prevents, and does so precisely enough to name the
victim clone.

### Hard rules

- **Cardinality is not identity.** "Exactly one session connected" never authorizes a bind
  (F2–F4). A silent rebind on count is the single worst failure this plan exists to prevent.
- **Non-circularity.** Expected values (nonce, source hash) come from this clone's disk via the
  `execute_luau` argument; observed values come from the Rojo-synced DataModel. Never derive the
  expected side from synced source, or the guard only proves Rojo agrees with itself.
- **Liveness ≠ sufficiency.** A fresh nonce proves a live Rojo link, not that *this migration's
  file* arrived. F19 guarantees stale baked copies survive. The guard must compare the source.
- **Absent ≠ pass.** Wherever a value is compared (nonce, `up`, `down`, hook, receipt), absence on
  either side is a refusal.
- **Per-clone-divergence tripwire.** Any control whose *enablement* lives in `.git/config`, a
  shell profile, an editor setting, or the developer's memory is divergent by construction and
  needs a self-healing installer on a guaranteed path. That path is `rojo-up` (D0). F10 and F24
  are both instances of this failure.

posts.cooked:
---
  Studio Session Safety — how we bind AI tooling to the right Studio window

  The setting. We develop one Roblox place from several parallel git clones, each on its own branch, each with its own rojo serve and
  its own Studio window open on the same place — often concurrently. An AI coding agent drives Studio through the Studio MCP server
  (execute_luau, etc.). Every MCP call takes a studio_id, but that id is only a handle to a Studio process — it cannot tell you which
  clone's Rojo feed that window is on. If a write lands in the wrong window, the developer later hits File > Save, the wrong clone's
  place file absorbs it, and it gets committed. Nothing errors at any point. That silent cross-clone write is the failure the system
  exists to prevent.

  Why the obvious discriminators don't work (all measured, not assumed):

  - list_roblox_studios names are byte-identical for two windows on the same place, and game.PlaceId / GameId are identical too —
  every clone is the same place. (A scratch-Baseplate test "proves" PlaceId works, because it reads 0 there; it's useless in every
  real case.)
  - The studio id's lifetime is the Studio process's lifetime — it survives place-close and Play/stop, so a cached binding stays
  "valid" until the developer quits Studio, long after the window may have been repointed to a different clone's Rojo server.
  - Cardinality is not identity. "Only one Studio is connected" never authorizes addressing it — a silent rebind on count is the
  worst failure mode, so it's banned outright.

  The mechanism: a per-operation nonce, proven inside the mutating call. No binding is ever retained — there is nothing to invalidate
  because nothing is stored. Each gated operation runs a four-step ladder:

  1. Rotate. A helper script writes a fresh random nonce into a file that Rojo syncs into the place (it appears as a StringValue
  under ServerStorage), and doesn't return until the nonce is verified live in this clone's Rojo feed via Rojo's HTTP API. Each
  concurrent agent instance gets its own slot file, so instances can't race each other. Freshness is per-operation: only a value
  generated after the operation began can match, so a nonce baked into a saved place file, or orphaned in a repointed window, can
  never authorize anything.
  2. Resolve. Enumerate every listed session; for each, read its mode from get_studio_state and probe the nonce read-only on the
  right datamodel — Edit in edit mode, Server during Play, never Client (a Client probe succeeds but sees ServerStorage empty,
  reporting "nonce absent" — a confident wrong answer). Each session classifies as match, match-in-play, foreign, or unreachable. One
  subtlety: a running playtest's ServerStorage is a snapshot from Play-start (Rojo keeps syncing only to Edit), so a Play session is
  also matched against a short history of recent nonces — otherwise a live window on this clone's own feed would silently drop out
  of the count.
  3. Decide on the count. Exactly one match in Edit ⇒ address it. Zero ⇒ refuse ("no window is on this clone's feed" — with
  per-session itemization, so "no Studio connected" and "a Studio is connected, but to another clone" stay distinguishable; they have
  opposite remedies). More than one ⇒ refuse — two windows genuinely on one feed is exactly the ambiguity only this outside-in
  enumeration can see. A match-in-play session is refused for writes, never retargeted: a write into the transient Play datamodel
  evaporates on stop while reporting success. Sessions are excluded only when provably inert (place closed), never merely because
  they're awkward to probe.
  4. Prove, in-payload. The mutating execute_luau opens by re-asserting the nonce and refuses itself on mismatch — addressing is
  treated as routing, not as a security boundary. For our migration system this assert also lives in engine code, so even a
  hand-typed command-bar run is covered.

  Two companion layers, because the nonce only proves whose scripts feed the window:

  - Source identity. Studio's edit-mode Luau VM caches require() by ModuleScript instance, and Rojo updates .Source in place — so
  freshly-synced source can verifiably be present while an older compile executes. Our migration runner therefore clones the module,
  hashes the clone's .Source, and requires/executes that same clone, so the bytes checked are provably the bytes run.
  - Save detection. File > Save is human, so the wrong-window save can't be prevented — but it's detectable: hash the local place
  file in every clone before and after a save. Only the one evidence-positive case (my file unchanged, a sibling's content-hash
  changed, and git activity ruled out) blocks the commit; every ambiguous case warns and passes, because a gate that blocks honest
  work gets bypassed and then protects nothing.

  Feedback for the Studio MCP team. The design would get simpler with any of: a per-session identifier tied to the plugin's sync
  connection rather than the process; any session-level field that survives to list_roblox_studios and is developer-settable (we'd
  put the clone path in it); and error copy that doesn't suggest choosing a session "by name" — for same-place multi-window setups
  the names are identical, and an AI agent following that suggestion binds arbitrarily.

  ---
